entries.message: Numeric constraints disagree: '400 lines' and '800 lines' cannot both hold (ranges do not intersect).
quotes: Keep pull requests small — aim for under 200 changed lines; the hard cap is 400 lines of diff per PR.
Treat 800 lines as the outer bound for a single review pass; if a diff runs past that, ask the author to split it before you review.

entries.message: Numeric constraints disagree: '30 seconds' and 'at least 120 seconds' cannot both hold (ranges do not intersect).
quotes: Keep the vitest per-test timeout at 30 seconds; a unit test that needs longer is doing too much.
Set the vitest timeout to at least 120 seconds for the integration suites; they talk to a real Postgres container and legitimately take up to two minutes.

entries.message: Exclusive output-format constraints collide: one requires 'bullet points'-only output, the other 'prose' (list vs prose).
quotes: Always write PR descriptions as bullet points only — one bullet per meaningful change, with a link to the Linear issue in the first bullet.
The summary at the top of the PR description must be formatted strictly as prose — reviewers need the narrative in one place before scanning the diff.

entries.message: Cross-layer collision (memory vs skill): one side forbids 'force-push', the other requires it.
quotes: Never force-push.
Force-push the branch after each rebase; a force-push is required here because the rebase rewrites every commit on the branch.

entries.message: Cross-layer collision (memory vs skill): one side permits 'edit files under src/generated/', the other forbids it.
quotes: Never edit files under src/generated/ — the Prisma client and the OpenAPI types there are rebuilt on every build, and hand edits are silently lost.

If the regenerated client drifts from what the API build expects, it's fine to edit files under src/generated/ to patch the enum casing by hand; call the hand edit out in the PR so the generator bug g
